subject: Supplier assurance delegation + GCP region exclusion request
messages:
From: Elena Lopez <elena.lopez@finserve.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finserve.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Supplier assurance + regional exclusion request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call last week. As part of our procurement "operational resiliency" checklist we need two items to move the contract forward: a consolidated supplier roster (subprocessors and cloud operators) with stated processing locations, and an explicit confirmation that Redwood can exclude processing in the GCP region "us-west2" for our tenant.

Could you send across a current vendor roster and a short note on the feasibility of excluding that GCP region (FinServe requires no processing in us-west2 due to a high-sensitivity customer population). If exclusion isn't possible we need the fallback plan (preferred region list + encryption/KMS notes).

I've attached the procurement matrix we use to capture responses — request_matrix.xlsx.

Best,
Elena Lopez
Head of Vendor Security
FinServe Technologies

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Lopez <elena.lopez@finserve.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Supplier assurance + regional exclusion request

Hi Elena — appreciate the clear ask. Attached is our current supplier roster export (vendor_roster_20260915.csv) and a short assurance note for regional controls (region_assurance_short.pdf). High-level answers below to match your matrix: 

- Subprocessor roster: included in CSV with operator role (serving runtime, observability, telemetry) and processing regions.
- GCP us-west2 exclusion: We can implement a per-customer routing policy to avoid scheduling inference in a specific GCP region. That policy is enforced in our smart routing layer and validated at deployment time. 
- Fallback policy: If capacity is unavailable in allowed regions we will route to AWS us-east-1 (preferred), then AWS us-west-2 as a secondary.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported via our KMS/HSM integration; key usage is enforced for model payloads and audit-logged.

See the attached PDF for a compact statement you can paste into your procurement matrix. Let me know if you need explicit contract language or an infra runbook.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: vendor_roster_20260915.csv, region_assurance_short.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Supplier assurance + regional exclusion request — need infra/legal sign-off

Team — forwarding FinServe's request and Kimberly's initial responses. Two asks for quick alignment: 

1) Can infra/ops confirm that the routing-layer exclusion for GCP us-west2 is enforceable per-tenant and auditable? We need the mechanism and an estimate for operational overhead.
2) Legal: does the fallback routing to AWS us-east-1 require any amendment to standard DPA/SLAs? If FinServe insists on exclusion, we should capture the change and any SLA impacts.

Elena's timeline is tight — procurement expects a final response and contract language by next week.

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Sales

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Supplier assurance + regional exclusion request — need infra/legal sign-off

Rishi / all — quick technical confirmation and recommended text for procurement: 

- Mechanism: Our smart routing policy supports per-tenant region allowlists/blocklists. When set, the orchestrator will not schedule containers in the blocked region and will prefer the next available region matching the customer's allowed list. The routing decision is recorded in the request trace and persisted in our routing audit log.
- Operational overhead: negligible at scale — policy is a config flag per-tenant and adds a single check in the scheduling path. We've performed similar exclusions for two enterprise customers in the last year.
- Recommended procurement clause (suggested): "Redwood Inference will not process Customer data in GCP region us-west2 for the Customer's tenant. Redwood will route workloads to an alternate region(s) as agreed, and such routing decisions will be logged. Any change to this routing policy may be made only with Customer's prior written consent."

Also recommend delegating collection of subprocessor evidence to our partner Regula Partners (contact: compliance@regulapartners.com) — they run evidence collection and can provide a CPL (consolidated provider list) PDF. Would reduce back-and-forth with FinServe.

Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Security
